therapeutic_hypothesis.compound: Metvix (methyl aminolevulinate) 160 mg/g cream with photodynamic therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.claimed_target: protoporphyrin IX accumulation in dysplastic cells
therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: methyl aminolevulinate is converted to protoporphyrin IX which accumulates preferentially in dysplastic cells and generates reactive oxygen species upon light activation
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: selective destruction of dysplastic skin cells while sparing normal tissue
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: organ transplant recipients with non-melanoma skin cancer
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: number of accumulated new skin lesions and complete response of actinic keratosis lesions

results.effect_size: significantly fewer new lesions at month 3 (mean difference 0.514, 95% CI: 0.116-0.911)
results.target_engagement_evidence: complete response observed in actinic keratosis lesions
subgroup_findings: Treatment area showed better cosmetic outcomes with less hypopigmentation compared to control area
Recurrence rates were higher in treatment area compared to placebo-PDT
safety_signals: Higher incidence of adverse events in treatment area (61 participants) vs control area (39 participants)
Serious adverse events included skin cancers, infections, and other malignancies

context.indication: non-melanoma skin cancer in organ transplant recipients
